limitations: Desktop IDE support validated on macOS Cursor 3.30.14; local CLI requires separate native acceptance. Cloud Agents are outside this support scope.
Public Cursor commands use /helix-<command>. Native /helix:<command> aliases and colon-prefix completion are outside this release scope; arguments are bound by the Skill entry protocol.

Telemetry requires explicit consent and a real current-session identity visible to the model. If host context injection is unavailable, statistics skip without blocking workflows. Missing or cross-stage tokens remain unavailable.
Automatic plugin updates require a Helix-managed local installation on macOS/Linux. Marketplace-managed or unregistered copies are not modified.

D2C uses an explicit checkpoint gate; no native skill-scoped Stop or user-question hook is claimed. An owner-bound completion requires the real current session identity; missing identity cannot be bypassed.

sessionEnd delivery/execution is best effort. Explicit consent revocation cleans this repository; a later sessionStart retries scoped cleanup while consent remains disabled. Closing a window does not guarantee cleanup.

Pinned native project installation is supported on the tested desktop build. Native automatic updates are unsupported; check provides current-installation facts and manual steps without consuming managed-local authorization. Statistics may remain partial.

Native Windows Cursor has no recorded acceptance session, so the POSIX sh hook launcher and the shell-quoted HELIXHARNESS_* identity prefix have no Windows evidence base; an unapplied prefix only skips statistics.
